sentences.text: Revenue compounded 6.2% a year from $26.6 billion in FY2016 to $45.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F157], but the path was a full cycle, not a straight line.
Revenue rose 25.6% in FY2018 [D93], with the Wirtgen acquisition adding 12% to net sales that year [P72], then climbed 23.9% in FY2021 and 16.5% in FY2023 to a $61.3 billion peak [D231][D322][F8].
It has since fallen 15.6% in FY2024 and 11.7% in FY2025 [D367][D412], a 25.4% decline from the peak [F8][F10].
The FY2024 drop came as rising grain stocks, lower commodity prices and elevated interest rates cut large and small agriculture shipment volumes [P17].

Production & Precision Agriculture was the engine, at 38.9% of revenue in FY2025 [D867], and it drove the upswing with contributions of +10.0pp in FY2021, +12.5pp in FY2022 and +9.5pp in FY2023 [D857][D860][D863].
That FY2023 gain came from volume growth and price realization of 17% in the U.S. and Canada and 12% outside it [P21].
In FY2025 the same segment subtracted 7.0pp from revenue growth as sales fell 17.0% [D869][D868], with U.S. and Canada volumes down 30% [P10].
Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue [D889], subtracted another 3.0pp in FY2025 on an 11.8% decline [D891][D890].

Operating income compounded 16.9% a year to FY2024 against 6.2% revenue growth [F159][F157], and EPS compounded 16.1% [F161] as the diluted share count fell from 316.6 million in FY2016 to 271.7 million in FY2025 [X110][X119].
Operating margin was 17.5% in FY2024 [F30], above the 12.1% window median but below the 21.2% FY2023 high [D1335][D1334].
Net margin fell 2.7pp to 11.0% in FY2025 [F50][D422], still above the 9.6% window median [D1338].
In FY2024 revenue fell 15.6% while operating costs fell only 11.9% [D367][D382], a 3.7pp gap [D389], as production costs stayed unfavorable on lower volumes and production inefficiencies [P16].
SG&A cost 10.2% of revenue in FY2025 versus 7.5% in FY2023 [D394][D304], and R&D 5.1% versus 3.6% [D393][D303], so fixed costs spread over a smaller base.
Below the line, interest expense of $3.17 billion [X82] and a 20.1% tax rate [D400] left net margin 6.5pp under operating margin [F30][F50].
Operating cash flow of $7.46 billion was 1.48x net income in FY2025 [F80][F40][D401], against a 0.91x window median [D1347].
The inflow was driven by net income adjusted for non-cash provisions and a decrease in sales receivables [P5].
Free cash flow of $6.10 billion was a 13.4% margin [F100][D398], near the 13.2% peer median [D1354], with capex at 3.0% of revenue and 0.61x D&A [D397][D403].
Management expects lower equipment-operations operating cash flow in FY2026, partly offset by inventory reductions [P6].
Net debt was $5.52 billion at FY2025 [D407], down from $35.8 billion in FY2021 [D226], or 12.1% of revenue [D408].
That net cash position ranks at the 100th percentile of seven industrials peers, whose median is -38.8% of revenue [D1357][D1358].
Buybacks and dividends of $2.86 billion were 46.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D409][D410], down from 121.9% in FY2023 [D320], and the share count fell 1.9% [D427].
Return on average equity fell to 20.6% [D411], below the 28.3% peer median [D1362].
Revenue fell in both FY2024 and FY2025 [R1][F9][F10], and the decline is broad: Production Agriculture, 37.1% of revenue, fell 17.6% [R2][D657][D658].
The filings attribute the volume drop to moderating market conditions and lower U.S. and Canada shipments [P10].
Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue, fell 11.8% in FY2025 [R4][D889][D890], and Small Agriculture & Turf profit fell on lower volumes and higher tariffs [P8].
The FY2017 SG&A figure was later restated to $3,098.0 million from $3,066.6 million [R8][X34]; the pack uses the first-reported value, so FY2017 cost ratios are slightly understated.
Watch whether FY2026 revenue falls below the FY2025 level of $45.7 billion [F10]; a further decline would extend the two-year contraction [R1].
Watch operating margin against the 12.1% window median [D1335]; a print below it would signal the cost base is not flexing with volume.
Watch free cash flow against the $6.10 billion FY2025 level [F100], given guidance for lower equipment-operations operating cash flow in FY2026 [P6].
